newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent firmer, Iraq, technicals pushing price.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent firmer, Iraq, technicals pushing price.

text.p: June Brent crude futures stayed firm into late trade on Friday, riding a modest wave of bullish sentiment built on worries of United Nations censuring Iraq.
June Brent was last traded at $18.47 per barrel, up six cents from London, while July was last traded at $18.55, up eight. Volume was 615 lots.
Brokers said a mixture of Iraqi news was helping build bullish sentiment. At the same time technically, the market was supported and appeared poised to test the upside sentiment.
"It's brewing. There is something to talk about," one broker said.

Various reports suggested Iraq could face censure by the United Nations, brokers said, including reports that U.N. monitors in Iraq had been arrested, Kuwait complaining Iraq vessels shot at Kuwait vessels earlier this month and Iraq flouting the no fly zone to pick up Haj pilgrims at the Saudi Arabian border.
June NYMEX crude was edging higher on ACCESS. June was last traded at $20.11, up eight cents from New York.
